concerns.text: T004's stated dependency is only 'T001', but its verification step requires 'applying all three methods to one filtered dataset' — a T003 artifact. The top-level execution order (T003 → T004) is correct, so this is an inconsistent per-task dependency annotation, not a true ordering violation; update the Dependency note to 'T001, T003' to match.

T006 and T007 are presented as parallelizable, but both append seed records to the shared file results/simulation_seeds.txt (T005 also writes there). Concurrent appends to one file is a hidden shared-state hazard if the braces are read as a parallel group. Either serialize them (T006 → T007) or specify per-task seed files merged later; neither carries a [P] tag, so at minimum clarify the braces mean 'either order', not concurrency.

T005's pilot writes data/results/type1_error_pilot.json while T007 writes results/type1_error/[stratum_id].json — two different result trees for the same artifact family, and data/results/ appears in no plan structure. Not an ordering defect, but the divergent producer paths will confuse the T008 consumer ('load all Type I error results'); consolidate the path convention.
